vBRIEFInfo.author: agent:deft-directive-setup
vBRIEFInfo.description: Add Smart-Git sidecar to ghproxy for git clone caching

narrative.Overview: Add WJQSERVER-STUDIO/smart-git as an optional sidecar to the proxy profile, enabling wjqserver/ghproxy's git clone cache mode. In bypass mode (current), ghproxy proxies git operations through to GitHub on every request. With Smart-Git in cache mode, git objects (blobs, trees, commits) are stored on disk and served locally for subsequent requests. Git objects are content-addressed and immutable, so they cache safely forever. Git refs (branches, tags) MUST always be checked against upstream before serving — stale refs are a correctness bug. Cache eviction must use LRU or size-based policy when disk fills up; TTL-based eviction of git objects is acceptable only if TTL > 24h. Smart-Git is added as a fourth service under the proxy profile. ghproxy config is updated from mode=bypass to mode=cache with smartGitAddr pointing to the Smart-Git sidecar. A smart_git_cache named volume is added for persistence. Depends on: fly-io-deployment (Smart-Git cache volume is allocated on Fly alongside the other volumes).
narrative.Traces: Item 4 from post-ship roadmap (git clone caching), FR-8 extension (ghproxy caching beyond file/release proxy)

items.title: Research Smart-Git API and config
items.description: Before writing any code: fetch https://github.com/WJQSERVER-STUDIO/smart-git README and config docs. Determine: (1) Docker image name and tag; (2) required env vars or config file format; (3) the HTTP API endpoint ghproxy calls (should match smartGitAddr in ghproxy config); (4) required volume paths for the cache; (5) any prerequisites (auth token, specific ghproxy version). CRITICAL — verify the cache invalidation model: (a) Does Smart-Git check upstream refs on every request (ref-based invalidation) or use TTL expiry? Ref-based is required — TTL-based that could serve stale refs is a correctness bug and is a BLOCKER; (b) What is the cache eviction policy when disk is full? LRU or size-based is acceptable; unconstrained growth is not; (c) How does it handle force-pushed branches (history rewrite)? The cache must detect the new ref SHA and not serve the old objects for the new ref; (d) Are auth tokens forwarded to upstream for private repo checks, or does the cache serve unauthenticated? If Smart-Git's invalidation model does not meet (a) and (c), do NOT proceed with the scope — document the finding and propose an alternative (e.g. shorter TTL, separate non-caching path for private repos). Document all findings as inline comments in the docker-compose.yml addition.

items.title: docker-compose.yml — smart-git service (proxy profile)
items.description: Add smart-git service under profiles: [proxy]: image (from smartgit-1 research), restart: unless-stopped, network gjgit, volume smart_git_cache at the path Smart-Git expects. Add smart_git_cache to the top-level volumes block. The service must have a healthcheck. smart-git should start before ghproxy (add to ghproxy depends_on).

items.title: configs/ghproxy/config.toml — switch to cache mode
items.description: Update [gitclone] section: mode = 'cache' (was 'bypass'), smartGitAddr = 'http://smart-git:{PORT}' (port from smartgit-1 research). This is a breaking change for existing deployments — add a migration note in CHANGELOG.md explaining operators must run docker compose --profile proxy pull && docker compose --profile proxy up -d to pick up the new Smart-Git service.

items.title: fly-compose.yml — smart_git_cache volume override
items.description: Add smart_git_cache volume mount override in fly-compose.yml, mapping to a Fly persistent volume path (e.g. /mnt/gjgit_smart_git_cache). Update scripts/fly-bootstrap.sh to create a gjgit_smart_git_cache Fly volume (10GB recommended). Only needed when the fly-io-deployment scope is also deployed.

items.title: Integration test: verify Smart-Git cache is used
items.description: Extend tests/integration/proxy.sh: after starting the proxy stack, (1) assert smart-git container is running and healthy; (2) run a git clone through ghproxy against a known public repo (e.g. a small public test repo); (3) check that smart-git's cache directory is non-empty after the clone (objects were stored); (4) cache correctness check: record the HEAD SHA before clone, then run a second clone and assert the checked-out HEAD SHA matches the upstream ref — this catches the case where the cache served a stale ref; (5) assert that the second clone is faster than the first (cache hit) by comparing elapsed time or checking that no new upstream fetch occurred. Teardown must remove the cached data. Add smart-git health endpoint assertion to the existing proxy health checks.

items.title: CHANGELOG.md and docs update
items.description: Add [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entry for Smart-Git integration. Update docs/high-volume.md: remove the 'git clone caching via Smart-Git is not included in gjgit v1' note and replace with instructions for enabling it (it is now included). Update docker-compose.yml inline comment on ghproxy service to reflect cache mode.
